The derivation begins with the foundational claim that every locally compact topological group admits at least one Haar measure. This is established by showing that if a Borel measure μ vanishes on some non-empty open set U, then it must vanish on all compact sets due to the compactness of those sets and the covering argument involving left translations. Left invariance ensures that μ(C) = μ(xC) for all x ∈ G, so if μ(U) = 0, then μ(C) = 0 for any compact C. Since compact sets generate the Borel σ-algebra, μ must be identically zero unless it is non-trivial. Thus, a Haar measure is characterized as a non-trivial, left-invariant Borel measure. The asymmetry arises because while left and right translations are mathematically symmetric, the definition privileges left invariance. This leads to the necessity of considering both left and right Haar measures for complete group-theoretic modeling in GSE and GSI.
